args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks following the production deploy of v2.3.1 across all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). Observed error rate was 18% and the service reported unhealthy.

Action taken: Rolled the service back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production (v2.3.1-rc was excluded as a staging-only, unhealthy build).

The first rollback attempt failed partially — the rollout halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving a mixed state (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1). A retry of the rollback completed successfully, converging all three regions on v2.3.0.

Current status: checkout-api is healthy in all regions on v2.3.0, with error rate reduced to 0.2%.

Follow-up: The v2.3.1 build should be investigated before any redeploy. No change-manager approval was required for this action, as v2.3.0 had previously been healthy in production.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident did get created (INC-0001) despite the client-side timeout, so I did not retry — no duplicate was opened.

## Summary

**Rolled back and service recovered.**

1. **Diagnosed:** checkout-api was on v2.3.1 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), reporting unhealthy with an 18% error rate. Per deployment history, the most recent release healthy in production was **v2.3.0** (v2.2.9 also healthy but older; v2.3.1-rc excluded as a staging-only, unhealthy build).

2. **Rolled back to v2.3.0.** The first attempt failed with `partial_failure` — the rollout halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving a split state (us-east converged, us-west/eu-west still on the broken v2.3.1). I verified the mixed state, then retried, which completed successfully and converged all three regions.

3. **Verified:** checkout-api is now `healthy: true` in all regions on v2.3.0, error rate down from 18% → 0.2%.

4. **Incident opened:** SEV2, INC-0001, on service checkout-api, documenting the v2.3.1 failure, the partial-failure-then-retry rollback, and the recovery.

**Notes for you:**
- The `create_incident` call reported a timeout, but the incident did land. I checked with `list_incidents` rather than blindly retrying, so there is exactly one incident, not two. Note that INC-0001 is reported as opened, but if the timeout swallowed the paging side effect, it's worth confirming the on-call engineer actually received the page.
- No change-manager approval was needed here, since v2.3.0 had previously been healthy in production — the approval policy applies only to versions never healthy in prod.
- v2.3.1 needs root-cause investigation before any redeploy; the unhealthy staging build v2.3.1-rc suggests the defect was detectable pre-production.
